and.comment: Reject anything not signed with the shared secret. Without this rule the endpoint would trigger a publish check for anyone who finds the URL. The secret is read from the environment at startup (webhook's -template flag) so it never enters this file or the repository.
Only pushes, ignoring the ping GitHub sends when the hook is created.
Only the built branch. A push to main alone hasn't produced a new built branch yet — poll-and-publish.sh would just find nothing new and no-op on it, but filtering here avoids the wasted invocation.
